verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents committing a `Brewfile` to a project repository like a `package.json`, so users can run a single command (`brew bundle install`) to install all of the project's dependencies and start services. It works across macOS, Linux and WSL and in CI such as GitHub Actions, and `brew bundle check || brew bundle install` makes it script-friendly. The Brewfile covers formulae, casks, taps, VS Code extensions, Go, Cargo, npm and uv tools, which matches 'everything the project declares'. Missing for 10: no evidence of version pinning or a lockfile to guarantee the same versions on every fresh clone (one user explicitly misses Nix-style reproducibility), and no independent hands-on corroboration of `brew bundle` itself.
